sources.entry: NSynth Super - AI experiment in sound.

summary.name: NSynth Super
summary.one_liner: An open source experimental physical instrument from Google's Magenta and Creative Lab that plays new sounds generated by the NSynth neural synthesizer from four source sounds.
use_cases: making music with new hybrid sounds
exploring machine learning in music performance
creating sounds that mix characteristics of several instruments
summary.what_it_does: NSynth (Neural Synthesizer) is a machine learning algorithm that uses a deep neural network to learn the characteristics of sounds and then synthesizes a completely new sound from them. Rather than blending existing sounds, it builds a new sound from the acoustic qualities of the originals, for example something part flute and part sitar. NSynth Super is a physical, open source experimental instrument that lets musicians play sounds generated by the NSynth algorithm from four different source sounds. It was built by Magenta with Google Creative Lab as an experience prototype and was shared with a small group of musicians to learn how they might use it creatively.
notable: Open source physical instrument built around the NSynth neural synthesizer
Creates new sounds from four source sounds rather than simply mixing them
Developed by Google Magenta with Google Creative Lab
Shared as an experience prototype with a small community of musicians
caveats: Described as an experimental prototype, not a finished commercial product
Page does not state hardware requirements, availability or purchase options
